messages:
matt_ops: Heads-up — since the BMC batch we pushed at 02:10 UTC, ~8 nodes in eu-west1 are flapping during OOB reconnects and flipping secure-boot state. GPU allocs are failing with 'node not ready' and autoscaler is spinning up on-demand in us-central, cost spike seen. 

sana_eng: Can you paste the logs? which rack/nodes?

leo_sre: Seeing same alerts. Heatmap shows provision failures concentrated on rack r12 (IDs 1007-1016). 

matt_ops: Logs from one impacted host: ```
[2024-03-15T02:12:04Z] bmc: watchdog: reconnect attempt 3 failed
[2024-03-15T02:12:04Z] nvram: secure_boot = toggled to 0x1
[2024-03-15T02:12:04Z] bios: boot-order changed: PXE -> SSD
[2024-03-15T02:12:05Z] gpu-provisioner: node-not-ready: KVM not responding
```

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oob-bmc-flap - recommended steps: reprobe, force secure-boot reset, pin fw.

sana_eng: Hmm. Looks like the BMC reconnect retry is triggering a nvram write path that toggles the UEFI secure-boot flag. That matches the boot-order flip. Not a pure network flap.

leo_sre: Immediate mitigation: drain the affected nodes from the pool so autoscaler doesn't spawn more replacements. `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and set node affinity to avoid eu-west1 fallback for now.

matt_ops: Doing a quick run: `oobctl reprobe --rack r12 --ids 1007-1016 --force` then `bmcctl nvram-reset --secureboot 1` on canary node (1007) only. Will watch.

deploybot: Notifying oncall @sre-oncall. Deployment event: bmc-fw v1.4.9 -> v1.5.0 at 02:10 UTC.

sana_eng: If nvram-reset keeps flipping back, we need to roll back the fw on the whole rack. But rollback is slow and touches 40+ nodes. Can we isolate the nvram write path with a patch?

leo_sre: For triage, set OOB health probe to failfast for r12 so we don't do partial writes. `oob-probe-config set --rack r12 --write-policy no-write` (temp).

matt_ops: Canary result: node 1007 reprobed, secure-boot reset to 1, rejoined provisioning, GPU alloc success for one job. Node 1008 still flipping.

sana_eng: That suggests intermittent BMC reconnect race. I've opened a PR with a small patch to serialize NVRAM writes on reconnect: https://git.internal/r/firmware/patches/542 - request urgent review.

leo_sre: Cost note — autoscaler launched 6 on-demand replacements in us-central as fallback, roughly +$9k projected for next 24h if not fixed. We should limit cross-region fallback while we triage.

matt_ops: I've set routing policy to prefer eu-west1 and limited cross-region fallback to 0 for the GPU queue. This will leave some queues waiting but avoids more on-demand spend.

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested maintenance window: 03:30-04:30 UTC for controlled rollback if patch doesn't land. Requires SRE+Infra + Dev oncall.

sana_eng: I'll prioritize the patch review. If tests pass, we can push a micro-firmware hotfix to r12 only (non-blocking full rollout).

leo_sre: Meanwhile I'll run a sweep to identify any other racks with similar hardware (same mobo revision) — list coming. 

matt_ops: Quick checklist: 
- disabled cross-region fallback for GPU queue (done) 
- drained affected nodes (1007-1016) except canary 1007 (done) 
- reprobe and nvram-reset on 1007 (canary green) 
- oncall paged (done)

sana_eng: If hotfix push looks good on r12 canary, we should schedule an expedited rollout across racks with same mobo revision and tag release with `bmc-fw:v1.5.0-hotfix-1`.

leo_sre: FYI I found two more racks with same board rev (r28, r33). I'll hold them from next scheduled fw rollout.

matt_ops: Postmortem note: add a test for nvram-write-after-reconnect to our firmware CI. Add a monitoring alert for nvram toggles >3/min on a rack.

sana_eng: Will add CI test and alert. Also filing a ticket for the release owner to update release notes about secure-boot nvram write race.

matt_ops: Thanks all. Keep updates here. If hotfix fails, we roll back v1.4.9 to r12 and schedule a full fleet rollback if needed. :thumbsup:
